_comment_1: Rule 6(1)(aa) LMPC 2011 - country of origin for imported products.
_comment_2: STEP 2. rules/INVENTORY.md called this 'the closest requirement to implementable - it needs one applicability input, not a new check type'. That input now exists: the 'imported-product' condition is declared per submission and is a REQUIRES link on this clause's RuleRequirement.
_comment_3: APPLICABILITY IS EVERYTHING HERE. A package DECLARED imported is checked. A package DECLARED not imported is recorded NOT_APPLICABLE. A package where import status was never declared reaches REVIEW_REQUIRED - it is NOT assumed domestic. Import status must never be inferred from the presence of importer_name: a package omitting both would then look exempt from a declaration it owes.
title: Country of origin for imported products
requirement: An imported package must state the name of the country of origin, or of manufacture, or of assembly.
legal_reference: Rule 6(1)(aa) of the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011
source_note: Checked 2026-08-30 by Claude Code (automated legal-source check) for raghavrrrao against the Department of Consumer Affairs consolidated publication 'Book on Legal Metrology Packaged Commodities Rules, 2011 with all amendments' (sha256 0ef948f9c6b89f5dfb20d384861901714fd0dc54fc67b5b86c772d2c3f983a4b; server Last-Modified 2025-04-14), via the verbatim quotation recorded in rules/INVENTORY.md. Clause (aa), inserted vide G.S.R. 629(E) dated 23 June 2017 w.e.f. 1 January 2018, reads verbatim: 'The name of the country of origin or manufacture or assembly in case of imported products shall be mentioned on the package;'. HUMAN COUNTER-REVIEW BY A NAMED REVIEWER IS OUTSTANDING, and the 2022-2025 amendment-chain gap in rules/SOURCES.md applies.
